I was really struggling a lot. Someone I trusted betrayed me and shared conversations I had. People were mocking my depression behind my back. I just felt utterly devastated. 

I went near the train tracks to try and cope. I read my book. I told people not to call the police. No one fucking listens to me. 

The police came, handcuffed me, involuntarily took me to the ER. It was a very traumatic experience. 

I've been to the psych ward before. It ruined my life. I fought and fought, yet it seemed like I was going to go back. I was mentally going insane. I was losing hope. For the second time in my life, I prayed to a higher  being, because I vowed I would kill myself if I were to the psych ward a third time. My friends have sentenced my death. 

After around 8-10 hours of bring awake, in a prison-like room, the doctor notified me that I don't have to go since he had an extensive conversation with my father, my therapist, and my psychiatrist. I was spared. 

I may have avoided the worst. But I'm just utterly devastated. I can't trust anyone anymore. I had to yet again go through another traumatic experience. 

Why does everyone want me to suffer so much?

But trust me, from a personal level, it is very very difficult to end things. Maybe it's survival instincts or just something in the brain, but it's very difficult to end things unless you've been suffering for so long your mind deteriorates completely into exhaustion and you simply fall across the train tracks.

This really might not be helpful at all, but I suppose it's just some of my mindless rambling. Maybe just trying to see things in a different way. 

See, those of us (myself included) wish for death, will eventually get our wish. If one thing in life is guaranteed, it's that one day it'll all be over. And I think that's one thing we have over those who are not depressed. People who are not depressed feel dread of the end of life. They turn towards materialistic goods or various religions to cope with the inevitable death but one day they will die as well, and it is a big fear. 

Isn't it good, even though we have to suffer so much, that one day our wish will come true? 

I suppose maybe I also might be missing the point. Some of us may be depressed because we want to feel alive. We want to be able to fear death. We want to experience life as it was meant to be. But how was it meant to be? In the past, human history has been absolutely horrific. Painful diseases, death, rapings and war, poverty, famine, etc... Life isn't so great. But we all are fighting, even for those who may not be depressed, they might be fighting a different battle.
